detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot begins from <Picture 3>: a medium shot of the driver's seat of the great waggon: a broad-headed clean-shaven man of about thirty in a black homespun coat sitting beside the driver with a brown-backed volume laid shut on his knee, the white canvas tilt behind him. The camera is on the powdery ground below the waggon seat, level with a standing man's eye and five long strides from the seat, a 50mm lens. The white afternoon sun stands high and a little behind the camera. The camera pushes in on the seated man across the whole shot, travelling two long strides as his hand comes off the brown-backed volume and rests on his knee at a normal walking pace, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 his head turns down toward the camera, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him a crowd of some thirty men and women in plain homespun stands back from the waggon wheel looking toward the seat, from 00:00 to 00:05.

Cloth, boots, wood and glass carry the physical action, and the movement and low murmur of the people at work nearby carry under it throughout.
